newsitem.title: USA: Cash grades steady in U.S. Gulf, outrights advance.
newsitem.headline: Cash grades steady in U.S. Gulf, outrights advance.

text.p: U.S. cash crude business in the Gulf started slow on Tuesday with only a handful of deals recorded at steady price levels.
Outright crude prices gained back all of Monday's losses and more, adding some 30-35 cents to move September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing to $20.20-30 a barrel.
NYMEX unleaded gasoline again led the way for crude, pegging price gains of 1.40 cents a gallon by mid-morning.
On the grade front, cash dealers said there seemed to be a lack of interest in moving barrels, with only one deal confirmed for Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James at 23 cents over the marker.
West Texas Sour/Midland talked around a $1.25 discount to September WTI/Cushing, steady from late Monday. Sour prices have fallen back from early yesterday when trades occurred at $1.10 under WTI.
Speculative buying came into the WTS market on word Canada's Interprovincial Pipe Line was to slice throughput some 140,000 barrels per day (bpd) in September.
